name: Wyoming
headline_status: Marijuana is illegal; only low-THC, high-CBD extracts are allowed for qualifying patients.
summary: Wyoming has no medical, decriminalization or legalization law for marijuana. Possessing 3 ounces or less is a misdemeanor punishable by up to a year in jail, and more than 3 ounces is a felony. A 2024 law (SF 32), effective July 1, 2024, bars adding synthetic THC or cannabinoids to hemp, which ended sales of delta-8 and similar products.

penalties.value: Possessing 3 oz or less is a misdemeanor (up to 12 months and/or a $1,000 fine). More than 3 oz is a felony (up to 5 years and/or a $10,000 fine).

medical_program.value: Only high-CBD, low-THC cannabis extracts are allowed, and only when a physician recommends them for a qualifying condition.

hemp_thc.value: SF 32 (2024 Enrolled Act 24), effective July 1, 2024, bans adding any synthetic THC or synthetic cannabinoid to hemp, and defines THC to include psychoactive analogs and isomers.

retail_sales.value: No legal marijuana sales; Wyoming lacks medical, decriminalization and legalization laws.

possession_limit.value: No amount of marijuana is legal to possess. Possessing 3 ounces or less is a misdemeanor (up to 12 months and/or a $1,000 fine); more is a felony.

purchase_age.value: No legal purchase of marijuana for any age; there are no licensed adult-use or medical marijuana sales.

public_use.value: Not allowed anywhere: there is no legal recreational or medical marijuana use, so using it in public or private can lead to possession charges.

tourists.value: No. There are no legal marijuana sales, out-of-state medical cards are not recognized, and visitors face the same possession penalties as residents.

home_grow.value: Not allowed; cultivating marijuana is a crime.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Wyoming has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis DUI requires evidence of impairment.

timeline.event: Gov. Mark Gordon signs SF 32, banning synthetic THC in hemp products.
